BOOKS numeral pass applied: 99 authored sentence rewrites across 11 book files. Leak-scan still CLEAN, check-data OK, book-budget D4 contradictions still 28, S8 still 0. KEPT eleven where load-bearing: ledger-leaf (the eleven names, sealed mystery), the-drowned-tally-eleventh-volume + the-soulrest-sheet (the eleven boxes, a declared contradiction pair), the-eleven-strokes-of-teeja-lun (title), crate-tally (the count dispute is the book), the-kiln-camp-order-book ('All eleven' - the sealed answer is 'eleven people who agreed to be forgotten'), and the three books carrying 'four hundred and eleven' (the Blackrose lease count, cross-referenced in game/data/quests/blackmarsh-coast.json 6x and game/data/states/ui-journal.json, and echoed by a sealed answer).

HONEST SPLIT ON RULE-39: Morrowind does not avoid the indefinite person, it spells it differently. -body forms ours 35.36 vs ref 0.27 per 10k (131x) BUT -one forms ours 14.78 vs ref 8.89 (1.7x). Pooled 'indefinite person' 50.13 vs 9.16 = 5.5x. So a -body->-one swap would have moved the one-token rule and left a 5.5x rule standing. Journal was worse: 292x on -body, 12.8x pooled. Dialogue: 34x on -body but only 2.4x pooled (dialogue's -one rate is 0.3x of Morrowind's, i.e. we UNDER-use it).
BOOKS indefinite-person pass applied: 127 authored rewrites (books-02 + books-03). -body forms 35.36 -> 0.00 per 10k; pooled indefinite person 50.13 -> 14.7 (5.5x -> 1.6x). RULE-39 books hits now 0.

RULE-21 (em dash) IS A GLYPH ARTEFACT, NOT A TIC — the single most important falsification of this run. Morrowind's text is ASCII and writes the dash as '--': books 20.37 per 10k, dialogue 19.04, journal 9.53. We write U+2014 and never '--'. Comparing the CHARACTER gives books 51x, dialogue inf (they have literally zero U+2014), journal inf. Comparing the FIGURE (any of — – -- ' - ') gives books 38.66 vs 21.87 = 1.8x, dialogue 17.69 vs 20.17 = 0.9x, journal 3.21 vs 9.85 = 0.3x. In dialogue and journal we use the dash figure LESS than Morrowind. Swapping — for -- would take a one-token detector from inf to 1.0 while changing not one word of the writing: it is the exact 'same fingerprint in a hat' move the brief forbids, and it is why the fix here is (a) report the confound and (b) trim only the genuine books over-use.

BOOKS dash pass: 35 line markers stripped by tools/prose/strip-line-markers.mjs (a dash used as a bullet/ledger rule is layout, not prose, and Morrowind never does it) + 14 authored layout rewrites. Books dash FIGURE now 24.46 vs ref 21.87 = 1.1x, i.e. parity. Did NOT rewrite the rhetorical asides: Morrowind uses the same figure at the same rate, spelled '--'. NOTE a real bug found in my own tool by its regression test: the first version matched an ESCAPED quote inside prose and silently stripped an inline dash out of marginalia-in-a-borrowed-book; fixed with a (?<!\\) lookbehind, dash restored, regression test added.

BOOKS round hundreds: 22 of 71 rewritten. The other 49 are load-bearing and enumerated: Blackrose arithmetic 529+411=940 (cross-referenced in quests), Knahaten dates 2E 560-601 (real series lore), ford casualties 151-vs-a-dozen (declared contradiction CF-060), tally-stone 41 notches/374 days, sixth-volume leaf citations, and the four-hundred-year span that is the spine of the chronology. RULE-08 in books is therefore a WORLDBUILDING concentration, not a machine tic: our corpus over-cites its own canonical numbers.

JOURNAL pass: 158 indefinite-person rewrites (incl. one shipped boilerplate entry duplicated on 24 quests) + 22 filler-number rewrites. -body forms 63.29 -> 0.00 per 10k; pooled indefinite person 77.74 -> 14.38 (12.8x -> 2.4x). Teens 127 -> 104 hits.

THE RESIDUAL 'ELEVEN' IN THE JOURNAL IS A DESIGN FACT, NOT A PROSE TIC — and this is the most interesting thing in the run. After the filler is gone, every remaining eleven is plot arithmetic a player can count: eleven live roots, eleven keepers at eleven wells, eleven burial boxes, eleven steps to the reservoir floor, eleven unwritten porters at eleven gold a week, eleven hundred in the box, 611 leased, 411 on the register, eleven names, eleven leaves in four hundred years. The machine's favourite number did not stay in the prose — it became the main quest's central motif. Renumbering it is a DESIGN change touching quests, states and a sealed answer, and is out of scope for a prose pass; it is flagged for the owner instead.

LIVE END-TO-END MUTATION CHECK (not just the self-test): injected 'There were eleven of them and nobody counted twice.' into 6 real shipped books on disk and re-ran the whole pipeline. RULE-01 4.69->6.09 per 10k, presence 12.9%->20.0%, acc 0.782->0.798; RULE-39 0.00->1.41, 0.0%->8.6%, 0.763->0.782. Reverted and verified zero occurrences remain.

RULE-22 (paired em-dash aside) is the SAME glyph artefact as RULE-21: 25.9x as registered, 0.9x/0.1x/0.2x orthography-normalised. Morrowind uses the parenthetical aside 5-10x MORE than we do in dialogue and journal.

TOOL BUG FOUND IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT: strip-line-markers.mjs v1 matched an ESCAPED quote inside prose as the start of a JSON value and silently deleted a real inline dash out of marginalia-in-a-borrowed-book. Fixed with a (?<!\\) lookbehind, dash restored, named regression test added. A tool that edits shipped prose and is only checked by the number it produces will do this again.

NOT FIXED, stated in report §9: RULE-36 contraction avoidance is now the LARGEST remaining signal and is bigger than 'eleven' ever was — our NPCs use contractions at 19.26 per 10k against Morrowind's 327.77 (0.06x) while using 'do not/is not/cannot' at 212.21 against 21.39. Morrowind's NPCs talk; ours read aloud. That is a dialogue-voice pass of its own, not a find-and-replace, because some speakers should be formal.
